issues.title: Terminal-time values substituted for quadrature history
issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting the iterated fully discrete scheme from the projected exact quadrature produces, in the kth summand, G(Pi_N U(t_k))-G(Pi_N U_k^K), together with the interpolation defect evaluated at U(t_k). The old definitions of both tilde Q_n and tilde P_n instead use U(t_n), and tilde Q_n also uses U_n^K, in every summand. Except for trajectories with constant nonlinear values, these terms cannot equal the displayed error recursion.
issues.overall_effect: The exact recursion on which the proof of ThmStrangFully is based is false, so the fully discrete error bounds are not established by the old proof as written. The theorem's rates need not change once the indices are corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the kth summand of both fully discrete defect terms, replace U(t_n) by U(t_k), and in the nonlinear stability term replace U_n^K by U_k^K. With these history values, the displayed recursion follows from subtracting the iterated fully discrete scheme, and the existing estimates establish ThmStrangFully with unchanged rates.
issues.why_classification: The outer index n is fixed while k is the summation index; the kth exact and numerical forcing terms, the semi-discrete analogue, and the subsequent history-norm estimates all uniquely force k. The proof never uses the literal terminal-time interpretation, so this is a systematic index-transcription error requiring no new inference or change of guarantee.

issues.title: Missing tau factor in the discrete Duhamel corollary
issues.failure_explanation: Fix T>0, take f=g=0, and let F_k=h be a nonzero spatial constant for 0≤k≤floor(T/tau), with F_k=0 otherwise. On the zero Fourier mode, the first component of exp((n-k)tau A)(0,h) is (n-k)tau h. Thus the old unweighted sum is of size 1/tau over a fixed positive portion of the time interval, so its discrete ell^p_tau norm is also of order 1/tau, whereas the stated ell^1_tau forcing norm stays of order one. The proof's analogy with continuous Duhamel therefore supports the tau-weighted sum appearing in the new version, not the old definition.
issues.overall_effect: CorDisStrichWave is false as stated. Its use at the (6,9) Strichartz pair in LemDiskrWellp is unsupported, which propagates through LemStabStrang4 to the alpha=4 portions of the semi-discrete and fully discrete convergence theorems.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the discrete Duhamel sequence with the quadrature weight, W_n = exp(nτA)(f,g) + τ sum_{k=0}^n exp((n-k)τA)(0,F_k), and apply the discrete Strichartz argument to this weighted convolution. Check the recorded dependents using their existing τ-weighted discrete Duhamel formulas; LemDiskrWellp, LemStabStrang4, ThmStrang, and ThmStrangFully then retain their stated alpha=4 rates.
issues.why_classification: The unweighted convolution is a well-defined statement making a substantively stronger uniform-in-τ promise; the zero-mode example shows that its sharp scale differs by τ^{-1}. Thus inserting τ is not merely a transcriptional or same-statement repair. Nevertheless, it is a contained correction to a recognizably comparable discrete Duhamel estimate, and every dependent application already has the required τ weight, so the affected chain survives without global reconstruction or major loss.

issues.title: Nonzero trapezoidal weight on the zero-length interval

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we allow here for general initial values $U_0 \neq U(0)$.

issues.failure_explanation: At n=0, the old discrete Duhamel formula reads U_0=U_0+(tau/2)G(Pi_{tau^{-1}}U_0), which is false for general permitted U_0. Correspondingly, the proposition's error identity reads E_0=E_0+(tau/2)[G(Pi_{tau^{-1}}U(0))-G(Pi_{tau^{-1}}U_0)], also false for a general initial value. A trapezoidal sum over the zero-length interval must instead have total weight zero.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition and its proof-level discrete Duhamel identity are false only in the expressly included n=0 case. The positive-step formulas and the convergence rates are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Index the trapezoidal weights by the terminal index and set c_{0,0}=0; for n at least 1 set c_{0,n}=c_{n,n}=1/2 and c_{k,n}=1 for interior k. Use these weights in the discrete Duhamel and error formulas. The n=0 sums then vanish, while every positive-step formula is unchanged.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine oversight in the degenerate zero-length interval rather than a mere transcription: the usual two endpoint roles coincide when n=0 and require an explicit special case. The repair is a short, routine local case distinction that preserves the proposition for all n, leaves all n at least 1 identities unchanged, and has no effect on the convergence rates.
